extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, and authors of narrative (non-systematic) review articles in medicine
extracted.subtask_description: A brief, six-item critical appraisal scale (SANRA) for assessing the quality of narrative (non-systematic) review articles, intended for use by editors, reviewers, and authors to rate manuscripts and guide improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of the review's importance (Item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the manuscript explains the importance of the topic addressed by the narrative review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated 0 (low) to 2 (high). Anchor definitions and examples are provided in the SANRA 'explanations and instructions' document to guide rating. Raters in the field test most often disagreed on this item, and the authors recommend rater training. A clear statement of why the review matters to clinicians/researchers scores higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of the aims of the review (Item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the manuscript explicitly states the aims or objectives of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated 0–2 with anchor examples in the explanations document. Clear, specific aims that frame the scope of the review receive higher scores. In testing, this item had relatively high agreement (one of the items with more frequent full agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of the literature search (Item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the authors describe how they searched and selected the literature (even if non-systematic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated 0–2. The scale expects some description of search methods/strategy appropriate for a narrative review (e.g., databases searched, search terms, selection approach). Item 3 showed lower item-total correlation and lower mean scores in testing; concise but informative descriptions score higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing (Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the adequacy and appropriateness of references used in the review (coverage, currency, and appropriateness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated 0–2. Anchor definitions/examples available in the accompanying document. Raters often disagreed on this item in testing, prompting clarifications in later wording. High scores reflect appropriate, balanced, and current referencing that supports claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific reasoning / presentation of evidence level (Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the scientific reasoning in the review, including presentation of the level/strength of evidence and logical argumentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated 0–2. The item covers whether conclusions are supported by the available evidence, whether evidence levels are acknowledged, and whether reasoning is clear and critical. Anchor examples provided to differentiate 0/1/2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of relevant and appropriate endpoint data (Item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the review presents relevant endpoint/outcome data appropriately and accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated 0–2. High scores indicate relevant, appropriate, and correctly presented outcome data that support the review's conclusions. This item had the highest item-total correlation in testing. Anchor examples in the instructions clarify expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring system and sum score interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the six items is rated 0 (low standard), 1 (intermediate), or 2 (high standard); maximal sum score is 12. The sum score is intended to measure the construct 'quality of a narrative review article'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors emphasize that SANRA is short by design and not a reporting guideline. There are no established cut-offs for quality grades, but the authors' experience suggests a score of 4 or below indicates very poor quality. Sum scores showed modest association with editorial acceptance in a small sample; use SANRA as one decision aid among others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater training and accompanying explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: The SANRA instrument is accompanied by an 'explanations and instructions' document containing anchor definitions and examples for each item, and the authors recommend rater training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors advise new users to train using the explanations document and to consider group training sessions. Training is important because reliability depends on raters' familiarity; disagreements were observed particularly for items 1 and 4. Use of the instructions improves clarity and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended use and limitations (scope exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: SANRA is intended as a brief critical appraisal tool for narrative (non-systematic) reviews; it is not a reporting guideline and does not cover all aspects of manuscript quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scale deliberately omits domains such as manuscript accessibility/writing (previously deleted), originality, and quality of tables/figures; these are important but outside SANRA's six-item core. The brevity trades breadth for feasibility in editorial workflow. Results (consistency, reliability) are study-specific and the authors recommend further field testing.
